first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because the venues keep sending her 'packages' and none of them look alike. The first paragraph says exactly that: same title, different wedding. Then it tells me rooms, transfers and outside suppliers are where they differ. That is where the money goes, so I'm reading on, top to bottom.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before paying any deposit.
journey.reaction: Before paying any deposit. Good. That's the sentence I'd have underlined for her myself.

journey.quote: Each includes a choice of beach or poolside venue, lanterns, petals and a floral table display, sparkling wine and cake after the ceremony and photographs from the hotel photographer, scaled to up to 10, 20 or 30 guests by option.
journey.reaction: Bouquets, lanterns, petals, wedding sweets. It's thorough, but this is my daughter's department, not mine. Up to 30 guests wouldn't even cover our side of the family. I skimmed this part.

journey.quote: Costa Navarino in the Peloponnese, Grecotel Corfu Imperial, Amanzoe, Santa Marina on Mykonos and Katikies in Santorini and Mykonos write a proposal on request rather than publishing package inclusions.
journey.reaction: By now I've lost count of the hotel names. On the iPad this section is one resort after another and I can't keep them straight. I'll let my daughter tell me which ones she actually likes.

journey.section: Civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic: the ceremony inside the package
journey.quote: One partner must be Christian Orthodox, both must be baptised Orthodox, Roman Catholic or Protestant, and the wedding is announced in a local newspaper at least eight days before, with approval from the Metropolis.
journey.reaction: Very useful. Neither of them is Orthodox, so that settles that before anyone falls in love with a chapel. Plain and direct.

journey.section: Civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic: the ceremony inside the package
journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only one issued in their own country.
journey.reaction: So which is it for Greece? I read this twice and I still can't tell whether the Australian one will do or whether we need the one from Athens. The acronyms don't help.

journey.section: Civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic: the ceremony inside the package
journey.quote: The Elounda Collection asks for each document to be Apostille-certified one by one and translated into Greek, emailed for approval at least four weeks before and couriered to the hotel at least three weeks before.
journey.reaction: This is the sort of detail I want, with dates attached. But it's crammed into one sentence. I'd like it as a little list with the weeks down the side so my husband can put it in the diary.

journey.section: Civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic: the ceremony inside the package
journey.quote: The marriage has to be registered by the couple at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days after the ceremony.
journey.reaction: A second step after the day. I'd never have known. And the note about a Friday wedding being registered on the Monday means they can't fly out the next morning.

journey.quote: Grace Hotel's fee includes transport between the hotel and the event site for guests staying at Grace Hotel.
journey.reaction: Good to know the guests staying elsewhere are on their own. But nowhere in this whole section, or anywhere else, does it ask whether Mum can get from the car to the ceremony. Terraces, beaches, a chapel 'across a small bridge'. Are there steps? Is there a lift? Nobody says.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms these in writing for your date before you commit.
journey.reaction: Someone accountable, in writing, before we commit. That's what I'm paying for.

journey.quote: Euphoria's packages "are complete packages, and their items are not interchangeable", with no refund or alternative for a service you skip.
journey.reaction: Thank you for saying it plainly. That's exactly the clause that catches people out, and it's money we'd lose without noticing.

journey.section: Venue package, planner or building your own
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing, one person. Good. I'd still want to speak to that person on the phone before anything is signed.

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: 10. **Deposit and cancellation terms.** What do you pay to hold the date, when, and what happens if plans change?
journey.reaction: Ten clear questions and the last one is the one I care about most. I'll print this list and give it to my husband. I'd add an eleventh: can an elderly guest get to every space without steps?

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: If one quote answers a point and the other is silent, the silent one is not cheaper. It is unfinished.
journey.reaction: Very good line. That's exactly how I'd look at a builder's quote.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: There is no agreement between Australia and Greece for free healthcare, so visitors pay for all medical care.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that. With my mother coming, this matters more than the cake. I'm forwarding this paragraph to my sister.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Wildfires occur in the extended summer from June to September, and heatwaves are frequent through the summer months.
journey.reaction: Honest without being alarmist. Heat is my real worry for Mum, so I'd lean towards May or late September after reading this.

journey.section: Compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian hours, Australian dollars. That ticks most of my boxes.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have step-free routes, lifts or level paths between guest rooms, the ceremony spot and the reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
For Greece specifically, will the Australian-issued CNI be accepted, or must it come from the embassy in Athens?
Who helps us gather, certify and translate the documents if that 'remains our task'?
Who reads the venue contract if it is in Greek or English legalese and priced in euros, and how is the deposit protected?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the ten-question list printed and the deposit and cancellation point circled
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the healthcare, insurance and heatwave paragraphs
My daughter, with the Orthodox requirements, so she knows the chapel option is out before she gets attached

cta_reaction.quote: When both quotes are on the table, compare your quotes with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: Fee in writing, AUD quotes and one person start to finish is most of what I want. I'd click if I knew a real person would ring me first, before anything is booked, and could tell me which of these places suit my mother's mobility.

top_3_changes: Add access for older or less mobile guests to the ten-question list and to 'What packages often leave out': step-free routes, lifts and distances between rooms, ceremony and reception. It is the one practical question the article never asks.

Break the legal documents material into a short dated list (CNI, Apostille, Greek translation, email four weeks before, courier three weeks before, register within 40 days) and say plainly whether an Australian-issued CNI is accepted in Greece or that this is the question to ask.
Trim the 'Island by island' roll-call of hotel names, or give each island one plain takeaway, so a reader on an iPad doesn't lose the thread before the useful sections.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing lines and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; turn_offs_found empty because no persona turn-off was genuinely triggered

open_questions.question: Accessibility for elderly guests is again this persona's main content gap (also raised on Crete). Adding it as an eleventh compare-quotes question needs no new venue facts. Treat as should-fix? Deposit protection, contract language, on-the-day contact and a phone-first step are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
